about: What the results page (../results_page.py) shows besides the checkers' results files (<checker>.json, written with --results): each jurisdiction's name and what it is checked against, in page order; the figures of those no checker here writes, from VALIDATION.md; every known difference, naming its contests by the checker's ids; and the US rules table. A contest that isn't exact and that no difference names is shown as unexplained.

causes.title: The ballot record isn't quite the ballots counted
causes.why: A few votes a candidate apart from the first round on, some over and some under, under every reading of the ballots tried.

causes.title: The official results checked aren't the final ones
causes.why: Only an earlier version survives in the Internet Archive.

causes.title: Ties drawn by lot
causes.why: Portland's code decides a tie for defeat by lot; this calculator uses a declared order, which chose the other candidate. Both elect the same councillors.

causes.title: Slips and gaps in the published sources
causes.why: Where the source contradicts itself or lacks what the count needs.

differences.text: Alameda County: 4 Oakland contests of 2024–2025, 1–7 votes a candidate.
Alaska: 9 contests of 2022–2024, first rounds exact, later rounds 1–9 votes a candidate.
New York City: 6 primaries, 1–33 votes a candidate.
Maine: the 2018 Democratic primary for governor, Janet Mills 3 votes higher in the last round.
Minneapolis: 2009 Board of Estimate, Becker 16,727 here against 16,728; every later round matches.
San Francisco: 2024 city attorney, district attorney and sheriff, captured 22–27 November, before certification on 3 December; 76–80 votes short.
Alaska: the August 2022 special for US House, the unofficial report of 31 August; 54–71 votes.
District 1: David Linn and Peggy Sue Owens, tied on 1,441.
District 3: Jaclyn Smith-Moore and Patrick Hilton, tied on 200.
Eastpointe 2021: round 4 gives Rob Baker 1,058.8175, 2 more than its own round 3 plus transfers; its round 5 builds on 1,056.8175, as here.

Cambridge 2019–2023: the records don't mark overvotes, so first counts are a few votes off and only winners are compared. The 2023 School Committee's last exclusion was King, 8 votes behind Harding; here it's Harding, 12 behind.
Scotland: of Wikipedia's 1,043 result boxes, 169 differ somewhere. Where an official source exists, the box is the one in error.

example.title: How a batch defeat lines up
example.intro: Many official counts defeat several hopeless candidates at once, or stop as soon as someone has a majority. Neither changes the rounds passed through, so each official round is required to be one of this count's rounds, in order, with the same candidates still in it. New York City's 2025 Democratic mayoral primary:

rounds.label: Round 1
rounds.text: Write-ins counted as one candidate: 1,581 votes.
rounds.after: Checked against the record's first choices.

rounds.label: Round 2
rounds.text: The write-ins go first, ahead of two candidates with fewer votes. That is this count's round 1, write-ins passed over.

rounds.label: Round 3
rounds.text: Nine candidates defeated at once. This count defeats them one a round and reaches the same two at its round 10.
